issues.description: setuptools<82 pin leaks build-tool constraint into the runtime install_requires contract.
issues.detail: The core package's hyperopt extra now requires setuptools<82 as a runtime dependency. setuptools is a build/packaging tool; pinning it in install_requires conflates the build-time abstraction with the runtime contract. Callers installing this extra inherit an unrelated ceiling. The right boundary is build-system requires (pyproject.toml) or CI scripts, not install_requires.

issues.description: Version-pin contract is undocumented and scattered across three locations with no shared spec.
issues.detail: setuptools<82 now appears in env_setup.sh, setup_mmcv.sh, and core/setup.py, each with its own FIXME or none. There is no single statement of the invariant ("until mmcv#3325 is fixed, setuptools must be <82 anywhere mmcv is built") nor a shared constant. When the upstream issue resolves, the contract for removal is implicit and easily missed in one of three sites.

issues.description: mmcv installed with --no-build-isolation silently widens the build contract to the ambient env.
issues.detail: Switching to --no-build-isolation means mmcv's build now depends on whatever setuptools/wheel/torch the ambient environment provides, rather than the isolated PEP 517 contract. This works today because the script pre-pins setuptools<82, but the implicit dependency on environment state is a leaky abstraction across CI runners and should be commented as such.

issues.description: mmengine and mmdet version bumps lack rationale in the commit boundary.
issues.detail: The diff replaces a pinned git SHA of mmengine (chosen for a torch 2.5 fix) with mmengine==0.10.7, and bumps mmdet 3.2.0 to 3.3.0. The previous contract (torch 2.5 compatibility via the SHA) is dropped without a statement that 0.10.7 satisfies it. A one-line note confirming the upstream fix landed in 0.10.7 would make the substitution auditable.

review.summary: The fix correctly unblocks CI by capping setuptools below the version that removes pkg_resources, but it spreads the same constraint across three locations without a shared spec, making the eventual revert path fragile. The most substantive concern is leaking a build-tool pin (setuptools<82) into core/setup.py's runtime install_requires — that crosses the module boundary between build-time and runtime contracts and propagates the ceiling to downstream users of the hyperopt extra. Secondary concerns: --no-build-isolation implicitly couples mmcv's build to ambient environment state, and the mmengine/mmdet version substitutions drop the prior torch-2.5 SHA pin without restating that the new pinned versions satisfy that invariant. No LSP violations or architectural rework needed; this is contract-hygiene cleanup on a CI hotfix.
